citation: Marion et al. (2017). A Practical Irradiance Model for Bifacial PV Modules. IEEE Photovoltaic Specialists Conference preprint; repository: https://github.com/natlabrockies/bifacialvf
description: bifacialvf is the national laboratory's Python model of irradiance on rows of bifacial photovoltaic panels. It calculates front and rear view factors for a five-row array assumed infinite perpendicular to the rows, with options for an edge row or single row and single-axis tracking. Inputs are row geometry, ground reflectance, module settings and typical-meteorological-year weather; outputs include hourly irradiance profiles and optional yield effects from rear-side mismatch. The represented site and year follow the weather file. The README states BSD-3-Clause licensing and provides PyPI installation and notebook examples, although GitHub's automated licence classifier returns no standard SPDX result. A limitation is the infinite-row idealisation, which may not describe short or irregular arrays. bifacialvf can support photovoltaic-generation estimates for grid studies. It complements PVDeg and other solar component tools by focusing on irradiance geometry. No weather file or module data was obtained.
inputs: PV array geometry and ground reflectance
